s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques, progressing over 2 months, in the context of immunotherapy
salient_findings: Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on her right arm
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
No new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Trial of oral terbinafine yielded no improvement
Biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation
Numerous eosinophils present on biopsy
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

differentials: Annular erythema associated with Sjögren syndrome
per_call: Annular erythema associated with Sjögren syndrome

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic annular erythema (EAE)
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils

shortlist.label: Wells syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of eosinophilic cellulitis and clinical presentation of pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques

shortlist.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques, although less likely due to lack of scale and negative PAS stain

shortlist.label: Granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of annular plaques, although less likely due to presence of numerous eosinophils on biopsy

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy findings of superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils, consistent with eosinophilic cellulitis

raw.rationale: The presence of numerous eosinophils on biopsy and the clinical presentation of erythematous annular plaques without scale, which started as a papule and gradually enlarged and spread, are consistent with Eosinophilic annular erythema (EAE). The lack of response to antifungal treatment and the negative PAS stain for fungal organisms also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Wells syndrome
rejected.why: While Wells syndrome also presents with eosinophilia, it typically has a more acute onset and is often associated with systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Erythema annulare centrifugum
rejected.why: This condition can present similarly, but the presence of numerous eosinophils on biopsy is more characteristic of Eosinophilic annular erythema (EAE).

rejected.label: Granuloma annulare
rejected.why: The biopsy findings do not show the characteristic granulomatous inflammation of Granuloma annulare, and the clinical presentation is not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic cellulitis
rejected.why: Eosinophilic cellulitis is another term for Wells syndrome, which has already been considered and rejected due to the lack of systemic symptoms and the clinical presentation.
